confirmed_boundary: A run 38185461370 failed opening the owned browser WebSocket after endpoint record and Chrome process/profile ownership validation succeeded. Native sign-in and Notes interactions were never reached.
cause: Undetermined; current evidence cannot distinguish Chrome handshake latency, Node WebSocket-specific failure, and event-loop starvation. No timeout, retry, resource gate, browser argument or product code was changed.

experiment.launch_authority: Parent coordinator only; no hosted run launched by this lane.
experiment.activation: Use the new default-false hosted workflow notes_startup_diagnostic=true input on the explicitly authorized notes-find-member lane A run. Actual lane admission rejects enabling it for any other case or lane. Acceptance maps MATRX_CDP_STARTUP_DIAGNOSTIC=1 only for that input/case/lane; the native harness enables both the existing process CPU bracket and new owned-CDP phase receipt. SEO resource diagnostics retain their prior input, admission and CPU-only behavior.
experiment.peer_round_one: Fresh peer rejected the original activation claim: seo_resource_diagnostic is guest-seo/full/airbnb-only, so it could not lawfully enable this on Notes. Corrected with a separate Notes input and an executable workflow-to-native routing test; no hosted retry launched.
experiment.ordinary_mode: Disabled by default; passes identical options to the original connector without timers, process reads, or extra loopback handshakes.
experiment.measurement: BROWSER_CDP_STARTUP_INTERVAL records relative endpoint-read, owner-check, owner-verified, socket-constructed, socket-open/error, close-requested/closed and connector-settled times; timer sample count and maximum lateness; independent TCP-connect and HTTP Upgrade numeric status. The independent request begins only after the real connector validates owned Chrome identity and profile.
experiment.privacy: No endpoint URL, port, path, headers, body, auth, process arguments or exception text is emitted. Only fixed categories, durations, counts and HTTP status numbers leave the helper.
experiment.limits: The diagnostic probe and timer are stopped when the original connector settles. No retry, wider timeout, new admission decision or product acceptance result is introduced. The probe can affect an already failing Chrome slightly; it is opt-in and evidence is diagnostic only.

predictions.distinguishing_observation: Large timer lateness aligned with the open/close boundary; compare the existing CPU process bracket for owned Node versus external/Chrome work. Timely timers would weaken this hypothesis.

predictions.hypothesis: Chrome listener accepts TCP but cannot complete a browser WebSocket handshake
predictions.distinguishing_observation: Independent TCP-connect occurs, but neither independent 101 Upgrade nor native socket-open appears while Node timers remain timely. A prompt independent 101 would weaken this hypothesis.
Independent handshake returns 101 promptly while native socket never opens and timers remain timely. If both transports stall this hypothesis loses support.

predictions.hypothesis: Reported startup duration inflated by socket-close cleanup
predictions.distinguishing_observation: Close-requested precedes connector-settled by approximately the unchanged cleanup budget; separate the open wait from cleanup in the receipt.

experiment.interpretation_limit: A CPU bracket establishes activity during the interval, not sole causation. If both transports stall without event-loop delay, the evidence localizes Chrome/loopback; it does not by itself prove an external host CPU cause.
